item.research_question: How do surface conditions (clean vs. oxidized/passivated) influence the deformation mechanisms and mechanical behaviors of lead (Pb) nanocrystals?
item.material_system: Pb nanoparticles (diameters < 25 nm) and surface-passivated Pb particles with PbOx layers
item.processing_route: In situ heat treatment of PX-PbTiO3 nanowires at 350°C under electron beam irradiation (beam density ~4×10^4 A/m^2) to form Pb particles; surface passivation achieved by prolonged electron beam irradiation (~10 minutes) to form PbOx layers; mechanical testing using electrochemically etched W tips (2.5 V, 20 mA NaOH etching) at ~0.3 nm/s inside an aberration-corrected FEI Titan 80-300 TEM
item.test_conditions: In situ mechanical compression and stretching inside an aberration-corrected TEM at room temperature (implied by lack of heating during test), with particle sizes ranging from ~11.7 nm to 16.7 nm
key_findings: 78% of clean Pb particles exhibited dominant diffusive pseudoelastic deformation, while only 22% showed displacive plasticity.
100% of surface-passivated Pb particles demonstrated displacive plastic deformation with no pseudoelasticity.
A threshold particle diameter of 67 nm was derived below which diffusive deformation overwhelms displacive deformation in pure Pb.
Clean Pb particles recovered their initial ellipsoid shape after compression and stretching due to surface atom diffusion.
Surface-passivated Pb particles retained irregular shapes after unloading due to suppressed diffusion and dominant plasticity.
Twinning and stacking fault formation were more favored in surface-passivated particles compared to clean particles.
Surface passivation increased the stress required to drive plastic deformation, as seen in half-passivated particles where the clean segment stretched while the passivated segment remained stable.
item.mechanism: In clean Pb nanoparticles, surface atom diffusion dominates and drives pseudoelastic deformation by minimizing surface energy. In surface-passivated particles, the PbOx layer inhibits surface diffusion, forcing deformation to proceed via displacive mechanisms such as dislocation slip, stacking faults, and twinning, which result in irreversible plastic deformation.
item.limitations: The study focuses specifically on Pb; the authors note that the surface condition effect is expected to be most prominent in active metals with small sizes and good surface diffusivities (e.g., Cu, Bi, Sn, Ag), implying generalizability to other metals requires further verification.
item.future_work: The authors propose that surface engineering can be used to tune the mechanical properties of small-volume metals and suggest investigating the surface condition effect in other active metals like Cu, Bi, Sn, and Ag.
quotes: In most of the pristine Pb particles, surface atom diffusion dominates and leads to a pseudoelastic deformation behavior.

In stark contrast, in surface-passivated Pb particles where surface atom diffusion is largely inhibited, deformation proceeds via displacive plasticity including dislocations, stacking faults, and twinning.
Surface passivation also increases the stress required for driving plastic deformation.
